references.text: God tells Abraham about the future of his descendants, including slavery in Egypt and the promise of return, which provides the immediate context for verse 16.
The Israelites' stay in Egypt lasted 430 years, corresponding to the timeframe implied by God's promise of return in the fourth generation.
The land became unclean because of the sins of its inhabitants, and God punished them—directly relevant to the statement that the Amorites' sin was not yet complete.
God explains that it is not Israel's righteousness but the wickedness of other nations that is the reason they receive the land—in line with the principle of the Amorites' sin in Gen 15:16.
The idolatry and wickedness of the Amorites are mentioned as an example, clarifying what kind of sin is referred to in Gen 15:16.
God promises to bring His people out of Egypt into a good land, away from among others including the Amorites—a fulfillment of the promise of return.
By faith Abraham lived in the promised land as a foreigner, trusting in God's promises that his descendants would one day inherit it.
